target_customer: Enterprises in regulated industries such as finance and media that deploy generative AI and need policy compliance and auditability
problem: RAG, fine tuning and prompting are probabilistic and leave hallucinations and policy violations. CTGT edits model behavior at the representation layer and turns policies into enforceable constraints without retraining.
business_model: Enterprise software and platform licensing with self hosted open source models; pricing not public
product_category: AI reliability and interpretability, policy engine for LLMs

founders.name: Cyril Gorlla
prior_employers: Intel (ML telemetry collaboration, per YC page)
education: UC San Diego and Stanford research, left to found CTGT (per YC page, no degree listed)
founders.background_notes: Business Insider headline describes him as 23 when funding was reported.

founders.name: Trevor Tuttle
education: UC San Diego deep learning research (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Co-founder named in funding coverage; YC page gives first name only.

technical_complexity.rationale: Productizing representation engineering and mechanistic interpretability to intervene in model internals was research grade work in 2024 for a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary methods and research lead, but model labs and interpretability groups could build similar controls.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found on model labs absorbing this wedge; incumbent names are a judgment.

market_need_then: Regulated enterprises were slowed in deploying generative AI by hallucination and compliance risk; TechCrunch covered CTGT at Disrupt in October 2024 on making models safer.

branding.name_origin: Funding coverage (via a search summary of press) says the name comes from founders' initials; not confirmed in an opened source.
branding.community_and_virality: Press on the founder age story (Business Insider) and a Forbes CES list mention on its site; no community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Acronym is hard to say and confuse with CTG companies in search, but enterprise buyers rely on credibility more than name.

outcome_analysis: CTGT raised a 7.2M dollar seed in early 2025 led by Gradient Ventures after YC Fall 2024 and a Disrupt appearance, and claims Fortune 500 deployments. Strength comes from research depth and the compliance wedge; risks are model labs adding native controls and long enterprise sales cycles. No exit or distress was found.
notes: Round cross checked between Gradient's own post and Business Insider. Some aggregators date the round to 2024-10; press says 2025-02. Company description on YC says 8M seed, press says 7.2M, so the larger figure is unverified. No competitor source dated near the batch was found, so the list is empty. No later rounds found.
